queries.protein_name: Guanosine 5'-monophosphate reductase (MsmGMPR) tetramer - flap region in open vs closed conformations
queries.paper_title: Structural basis for allosteric regulation of mycobacterial guanosine 5´-monophosphate reductase by ATP and GTP.
queries.source_panel_mapping: Figure 7 a-d (four ligand states) + e (overlay of open and closed flap/CBS)
queries.caption: Changes in the flap region induced by ligand binding.In the ribbon representations, only the flap region (magenta, residues 381–420), the CBS domain from the opposite tetramer (blue, residues 97–206), and the bound ligands (coloured by heteroatoms) are displayed. In the tube representations, the flap regions are shown in magenta, the first tetramer in green, and the second (opposite) tetramer in blue. Structures were superimposed on chains A and D. a–d Conformations of the flap region and the position of the CBS domain from the opposite tetramer in MsmGMPR: a without any ligand (PDB ID: 7OY9); b with GMP in the active site and GTP in binding site G (PDB ID: 8RY3); c with NADP+ and E-XMP* in the active site and IMP in binding site G (PDB ID: 9HG0); and d with GMP in the active site and ATP in binding site A (PDB ID: 9HG1). e Overlay of the flap region and the CBS domain from the opposite tetramer in MsmGMPR with NADP+ and E-XMP* (cyan), and MsmGMPR with GMP and ATP (yellow). The first red arrow indicates the area where the open conformation of the flap (cyan) and the compressed conformation of the CBS domain (yellow) overlap, making these conformations mutually exclusive. The second red arrow indicates the region where NADP+ (cyan) interferes with the flap region in the closed conformation (yellow). GTP and IMP are not shown in (b, c), respectively.
queries.pdb_evidence: Caption maps each state to an entry: 'In the ribbon representations, only the flap region (magenta, residues 381-420), the CBS domain from the opposite tetramer (blue, residues 97-206) ... a-d Conformations of the flap region ... a without any ligand (PDB ID: 7OY9); b with GMP in the active site and GTP in binding site G (PDB ID: 8RY3); c with NADP+ and E-XMP* in the active site and IMP in binding site G (PDB ID: 9HG0); and d with GMP in the active site and ATP in binding site A (PDB ID: 9HG1). e Overlay of the flap region and the CBS domain from the opposite tetramer in MsmGMPR with NADP+ and E-XMP* (cyan), and MsmGMPR with GMP and ATP (yellow).' Data availability: 'The atomic coordinates and structural factors for the X-ray crystallography structures generated in this study are deposited in the Protein Data Bank ... under the PDB accession codes 9HFZ, 9HG0, 9HG1, 9HG2, and 9HG3. The atomic coordinates of the cryo-EM structures generated in this study are deposited in the Protein Data Bank under the PDB accession codes 8RY0, 8RY1, 8RY3, 8RY4, 8RY5, 8RY6, 8RY7, 8RY8, 8RY9, 8RYA, and 8RYB.'
queries.source_notes: Textbook allosteric on/off figure: the same MsmGMPR tetramer is shown with the flap open in the ligand-free (7OY9) and NADP+/E-XMP* (9HG0) states and closed/compressed in the GMP+GTP (8RY3) and GMP+ATP (9HG1) states. Panels a and b are ribbon representations; c and d use tube/cylinder schematic renderings of the two tetramers; e is a ribbon overlay showing that the open flap and the compressed CBS domain are mutually exclusive. 7OY9 is a previously published X-ray structure; 8RY3 is cryo-EM from this study; 9HG0/9HG1 are X-ray structures from this study.
queries.caveats: Panel e overlays only two of the four states (9HG0 and 9HG1).

Panels a-d are ribbon diagrams of HsGPaLiv-AMP and the EcGP-EcHPr complex; panels f-h add the OcGPMus glycogen-storage site (6GPB), which is not part of the R/T comparison and is therefore not listed in pdb_ids.

queries.caption: eBDIMS2 simulates mechanistically smooth transitions also for complex and large-scale conformational changes.a Comparison between the quality of experimental end states, eBDIMS2 and MinActionPath2 transition points, and NOLB final frames for: (1) M. Smegmatis ATP synthase, from rotary state 1 (PDB: 7jg5) to 2 (7jg6); (2) Nf1 isoform 2, from active (7pgt) to inactive state (7pgr); (3) A2M, from native (7o7l) to activated state (7o7p). Distances between consecutive Cα atoms are reported using boxplot representations, considering n = 4684 consecutive Cα-Cα distances for ATP synthase, n = 4,830 for Nf1, and n = 5,074 for A2M. The bottom and top of each box are the 25th and 75th percentiles of the distance distributions, and the middle red line represents the median value. Whiskers extend up to the minimum and maximum values, while observations beyond the whiskers (red “+” signs) are considered outliers. b Synthesis cycle of M. Smegmatis ATP synthase simulated with eBDIMS2, generated by merging three trajectories: from state 1 (7jg5) to state 2 (7jg6), from 2 to 3 (7jg7), and from 3 back to 1. A cartoon representation of the cycle is provided (left) together with PC projections (middle). Graphical representations with arrows highlight PC1 and PC2 motions from the experimental ensemble (right). c Opening-closing motions of the three β-subunits (chains D, E, F) during the synthesis cycle, observed from the evolution of the angle θ between D59, K142, and L389 (right). Angle values are plotted along the synthesis transitions (left) so that dark blue spots (θ – 90°) correspond to closed β-subunit conformations, while bright yellow (θ – 110°) spots correspond to open states. Snapshots of β-subunit motions and c-chains of the F0 rotor are also reported (seen from the cytoplasmic side) for each end- and intermediate-state (bottom panel), showing the coordinated opening-closing motions of β-subunits and their coupling with the transmembrane domain rotation. queries.pdb_evidence: Caption: 'a Comparison between the quality of experimental end states, eBDIMS2 and MinActionPath2 transition points, and NOLB final frames for: (1) M. queries.source_notes: Each panel pairs two experimentally determined end states (ribbon renderings of the deposited coordinates) with in-silico interpolated transition pathways - eBDIMS2/MinActionPath2/NOLB intermediate models - so the figure is classified as mixed. queries.paper_title: A dynamic structural framework for the allosteric regulation of Hsp70 chaperones
queries.caption: A dynamic structural framework for the allosteric regulation of Hsp70 chaperones.A, sensing of ATP. Cartoon representation of DnaK·ATP (4B9Q) with ATP coordinating residues as sticks in atom colors with carbon in the color of the NBD subdomain: dark blue, IA; cyan, IB; marine, IIA; deep teal, IIB (Movie S1). B, zoom into the ATP binding pocked with ATP coordinating residues as sticks. Overlay (NBD-IIA aligned) of apoDnaK (2KHO; sticks in white, labels in gray) with DnaK·ATP (4B9Q; sticks colored as in A). Graydashed lines are polar contacts between backbone amides and ATP and between residue sidechains; dark red dashed lines are polar contacts between residue sidechain functional groups and ATP. Arrows indicate the movement on ATP binding. C, ATP-induced conformational changes start in the NBD with docking of the interdomain linker into the lower crevice which brings the SBD closer to the NBD (1). Concurrently, the crevice is remodeled, presumably to stabilize the docked linker. ATP binding brings the lobes of the NBD together resulting in NBC closure (2) and full exposure of the interdomain interface to allow SBDβ docking (3). Once the SBDβ is docked, the lid domain of the SBDα opens and docks onto the NBD (4). On substrate peptide binding, the SBDβ-NBD interface is destabilized and the SBD may flip by some 180° (5) as shown in the crystal structure of the ATP-and peptide bound state (7KRU; (15)). The arrows above the equilibrium arrows signify increased (pointed arrows) or decreased (blunt arrows) weighted rates of the amino acid replacement variants relative to DnaKwt as indicated. The arrows below the equilibrium arrows indicate reduced total amplitudes relative to DnaKwt as indicated. Gray arrows in Step (1) refer to crevice remodeling and black arrows to linker docking. The green dashed equilibrium arrows in step (5) indicate that this step does not occur in DnaKwt in the absence of a substrate peptide (Fig. S3) but appears to occur even in the absence of a substrate peptide when amino acids that stabilize the SBDβ-docked state are replaced.

queries.caption: Structural overview of USP21 bound to a H2AK119-ubiquitinated nucleosome. (A) Cryo-EM reconstruction of USP21 bound to a H2AK119-ubiquitinated nucleosome (2.98 A). (B) Cartoon representation of model [zoom of the H2A C-terminal tail in (B)]. (C) The H2A C-terminal tail in our structure (yellow) is repositioned as compared to the crystal structure of an unmodified nucleosome (PDB: 1KX5, in gray) and is closer to the catalytic site of USP21 (blue). The last resolved H2A residue in our model (H2A S113) is shown for comparison. (D) Modeling of missing residues and isopeptide linkage of ubiquitin and histone H2A indicated by dashed lines and transparent model.
queries.pdb_evidence: Data and materials availability: 'The structure model was deposited in the PDB (PDB ID: 9NY4), and the cryo-EM density map has been deposited in the Electron Microscopy Data (EMD) Bank (EMD: 49919).' RCSB HEADER for 9NY4: 'USP21 BOUND TO H2AK119UB NUCLEOSOME' (ELECTRON MICROSCOPY, 14936 ATOM records), matching the figure title.
queries.source_notes: Panel B is the cartoon/ribbon representation of the deposited model. The caption also cites PDB 1KX5 (unmodified nucleosome crystal structure) as a comparison structure in panel C; that comparison entry is not this record's accession.
queries.caveats: The panel-D isopeptide linkage and some missing residues are modelled (caption: 'Modeling of missing residues and isopeptide linkage ... indicated by dashed lines and transparent model'), so parts of the displayed cartoon are built rather than directly observed.

queries.caption: Cryo-EM structure of the classical and lectin pathway C3 convertase.(A) Two views of the cryo-EM reconstruction of the C4b2a-C3 complex. Complement proteins C4b, C3, and C2b are depicted in blue, orange, and green, respectively, while the C3a/ANA domain is highlighted in red. (B) A ribbon diagram of the C4b2a-C3 structure accompanied by a schematic representation. (C) The interaction between C4b and C3 involves multiple MG domains from both proteins. (D) Interaction details between C3-MG4 and C3-MG5 and C4b-MG5 and C4b-MG4. Dashed lines indicate polar interactions including hydrogen bonds and salt bridges at distances less than 3.5 Angstrom. (E) Interaction between the C3 scissile loop and the C2a-SP domain, including enlarged views of the density map within the catalytic pocket on the top (red and green represent C3 scissile bond and C2a SP domain, respectively) and detailed molecular interactions on the right. In the right panel, C3a/ANA is shown in red and alpha'-NT in orange. The cleavage site is indicated by a black arrowhead. The oxyanion hole in C2a-SP is highlighted in blue, and the catalytic triad Ser679(A), His507, and Asp561 are highlighted in yellow. The hydroxyl group of Ser679 is depicted as hypothetical and is rendered in a lighter color.
queries.pdb_evidence: Data, code, and materials availability: 'Structural coordinates have been deposited in the Protein Data Bank (PDB) with the accession codes 9U60, 9U5Z, 9U61, and 9U62.' with maps 'EMD-63893 (C4b2 in loading state), EMD-63892 (C4b2 in activation state), EMD-63894 (C4b2a-C3 complex), and EMD-63895 (C3bBbP-C3 complex)'. Fig. 2 depicts the C4b2a-C3 complex, i.e. the built-in model deposited as 9U61.
queries.source_notes: Panel B is the ribbon/cartoon diagram of the classical pathway C3 convertase bound to substrate C3. Fig. 3B and 3E of the same paper contain further ribbon diagrams of the C4b2 proconvertase and C4b2a convertase (deposited as 9U60 loading state, 9U5Z activation state). Structures were built by docking published crystal structures (2ODP, 2WIN, 6S0B, etc., listed in 'other structural coordinates') into new cryo-EM maps, so all domains are experimental.
queries.caveats: PDB files here are the asymmetric/biological assemblies of the deposited models; the exact coloured cartoon in the panel may require symmetry expansion of 9U61. The independently deposited C4b2 loading-state model (9U60) is also downloaded for completeness. INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (partial): Fig. 2B depicts only the classical-pathway C4b2a-C3 complex, which is 9U61 (local TITLE 'CP/MBL PATHWAYS C3 CONVERTASE C4B2A AND C3 COMPLEX'). 9U60 and 9U5Z are the C4b2 proconvertase loading/activation states (ribbon views in Fig. 3B/3E), and 9U62 is the ALTERNATIVE-pathway C3bBbP-C3 complex of Fig. 4 (local TITLE 'AP PATHWAYS...'), a different complex and a different figure. Three of the four claimed IDs are therefore not the depicted structure of Fig. 2.

queries.caption: Cryo-EM structure of the FVa-APC complex. queries.pdb_evidence: Fig. 1A caption states verbatim: 'embedded model (PDB 9MOV) as a cartoon representation'; Table 1 'Structural parameters for the cryo-EM structure of the FVa-APC complex ... PDB ID 9MOT EMD-48481 ... PDB ID 9MOV EMD-48439'; Methods: 'Two models were deposited: PDB 9MOT (ab initio model associated with EMD-48481) and PDB 9MOV (flexible-fit model associated with EMD-48439).'

queries.protein_name: SNJ2 ORF19 (RepSNJ2) rolling-circle replication endonuclease — founding member of the new archaeal-virus/plasmid Rep-Arvir family (DUF7845 / Pfam PF25227)
queries.paper_title: A new family of rolling-circle replication endonucleases widespread in archaeal viruses and plasmids
queries.caption: ORF19 (RepSNJ2) and RepDE share a common active catalytic site. (a) Structural conservation between AlphaFold-predicted ORF19 (RepSNJ2) and a putative replication protein from Inoviridae sp. The 3D structural superposition reveals significant similarity, particularly within the N-terminal domain, between the AlphaFold-predicted ORF19 (RepSNJ2) (blue) and the Inoviridae protein A0A345MNV4 (gold). While the structural similarity was initially identified by Foldseek, the quantitative structural alignment performed using TM-align yielded an RMSD of 4.67 Å and a TM-score of 0.54, confirming a highly conserved global topological fold. (b) Crystal structure of RepDE1 (PDB ID: 4CWC) and the AlphaFold-predicted ORF19 (RepSNJ2) structure. Quantitative structural alignment of the core domains using TM-align yielded an RMSD of 4.47 Å and a TM-score of 0.49. The conserved catalytic tyrosine (Y191) and the three metal-coordinating residues (D46, D142, and E214) essential for its activity are colored (Y, red; D, yellow; E, orange). The corresponding conserved residues in the ORF19 (RepSNJ2) structure are labeled with the identical color scheme, demonstrating the precise spatial conservation of the catalytic center. (c) WebLogo representations of the conserved Motif III of Rep_trans protein family (consensus: YxxK/YxxKY) and DUF7845 containing homologs. The left panel shows the motif in the Rep_trans protein family, and the right panel shows the corresponding motif in DUF7845 containing homologs. Amino acid residues are colored by chemical property. (d) Functional analysis of ORF19 (RepSNJ2) active-site mutants. Transformation efficiencies in J7-3-F were measured for plasmids expressing ORF19 (RepSNJ2) variants. Mutations targeted key predicted functional sites: (i) the catalytic motif, including the essential tyrosine (Y283A and Y283F) and surrounding conserved residues (K281A, H282A, Y284A, M285A); (ii) conserved acidic residues predicted for metal ion coordination (E25A, D207A, E303A); (iii) conserved residues within the C-terminal DNA-binding domain (D408A, G409A, G410A). Data represent the mean of three biological replicates, with error bars indicating standard deviation. (e) Structural superposition of the putative HTH d7omains of SNJ2 ORF19 (accession: YP_010 772 542, truncated, 395–469, left) and the HHPV3 ORF19-like protein ORF11 (accession: YP_009 798 574, truncated, 376–466, center) with MarR family regulator from E. coli (PDB: 1JGS, truncated, 38–125, right) [78]. (f) Schematic of the domain organization of ORF19 (RepSNJ2). Positions of conserved motifs are noted.
queries.pdb_evidence: Figure 4 caption: “(b) Crystal structure of RepDE1 (PDB ID: 4CWC) and the AlphaFold-predicted ORF19 (RepSNJ2) structure.” The RepSNJ2/ORF19 model itself is AlphaFold-predicted in this work (no experimental coordinates deposited for it); 4CWC is the previously determined experimental RepDE structure used for comparison. 4CWC = “Structure of Rolling Circle Replication Initiator Protein (RepDE) from Staphylococcus aureus” (X-ray, 2.9 Å).
queries.source_notes: Panel a superposes the AlphaFold-predicted ORF19 (RepSNJ2, blue) with an AlphaFold model of an Inoviridae replication protein (gold); panel b superposes the experimental crystal structure of RepDE (PDB 4CWC) with the predicted ORF19 and highlights the conserved catalytic tyrosine and metal-coordinating residues. This is an AlphaFold-based new-family assignment for a viral 'dark matter' protein, so it is recorded as mixed/predicted rather than as an experimental structure.
queries.caveats: No experimental structure of RepSNJ2/ORF19 exists in this paper; the ribbon model of the protein of interest is AlphaFold-predicted. Only the comparison structure 4CWC is experimental, and its .pdb file was downloaded and validated. INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (partial): Fig. 4b caption does name 4CWC, but 4CWC is the previously published S. aureus RepDE crystal structure used as a superposition comparison; the record's claimed subject (SNJ2 ORF19) is an AlphaFold model with no deposited coordinates. The ID is a comparison structure, not the depicted subject.

queries.caption: Molecular footprints of the 4 major antigenic sites on Ara h 2c and Ara h 6c. (A) Ribbon diagram (left) and molecular surface of Ara h 6c showing the surfaces buried from solvent in 16A8 (red), 13D9 (orange), 1H9 (yellow), and 8F3 (green). queries.pdb_evidence: “The structures have been deposited in the Protein Data Bank under accession codes 8SHV, 8SHW, 8SJ6, 8SI1, 8SJ4, and 8SJA.” Table E1 maps each code to its complex: 38B7 = 8SHV; 38B7_PepOH = 8SHW; AraH2-8F3-38B7 = 8SJ6; AraH6-16A8 = 8SI1; AraH6-8F3-1H9 = 8SJ4; AraH6-13D9-16A8 = 8SJA. (A) Ribbon diagram (left) and molecular surface of Ara h 6c showing the surfaces buried from solvent in 16A8, 13D9, 1H9, and 8F3 ... (C) Ribbon diagram ... of Ara h 2c.” Panels A and B depict the Ara h 6c complexes (8SI1, 8SJA, 8SJ4) and panel C the Ara h 2c complex (8SJ6); 8SHV and 8SHW are the two 38B7 Fab-Ara h 2.01 complexes from the same deposition.
queries.caveats: Residue numbering in the caption excludes secretion signals. All six deposited structures are Fab-allergen complexes, so the downloaded files contain antibody heavy/light chains in addition to the allergen; the allergen is the ribbon-diagram component highlighted in the figure. The image is the author-manuscript figure file served from the PMC OA bucket. INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (partial): Fig. 5 footprints derive from 8SI1 (Ara h 6-16A8), 8SJA (Ara h 6-13D9-16A8), 8SJ4 (Ara h 6-8F3-1H9) and 8SJ6 (Ara h 2-38B7/8F3); 8SHV (38B7 unliganded) and 8SHW (38B7 + hydroxy-proline peptide) are Fab-only structures shown in Figs 3-4, not Fig. 5. The latter two are not attributable to this figure.

queries.pdb_evidence: Figure 2 caption: 'Superimposition of the AI-predicted ALAD structures, generated using ESM (blue), AF2 (purple), AF3 (green), and RF (red), onto the original crystal structure of ALAD (yellow; PDB ID: 2Z1B, chain B).' Panels A and B are pLDDT / predicted-Angstrom-error confidence plots (no coordinates). queries.caveats: 2Z1B is the experimental structure the predicted models are superposed onto, not a predicted model. No PDB accession exists for the ESMFold/AF2/AF3/RoseTTAFold models. Figure 3/5 of the same paper also show PDB 1E51 (human ALAD-porphobilinogen) and the rebuilt 'RE-ALAD' model; those are different figures and are not part of this record. INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (partial): 2Z1B is a previously deposited structure that serves only as the superposition reference for the AI-predicted ALAD models that are Fig. 2's actual subject (the paper obtained 2Z1B coordinates from the PDB and deposited no new coordinates). The record matches protein and caption, but the claimed ID is a prior/reference structure.

INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (partial): 6UB6 is the Lentinula edodes LeGLU1 crystal structure used as the ColabFold homology template (Methods) and shown as the panel C comparison; the record's subject GlGH128A is a predicted model with no PDB entry, and the panel C caption does not name the ID.

(A) Structure of 8TRB used as a template for hP2X7 model construction, with its three subunits highlighted in blue, green, and orange. (B) Predicted Q99572–8TRB (hP2X7_closed) model generated by SWISS-MODEL, with subunits highlighted in pink, blue, and green. (C) Structural superposition between the predicted Q99572–8TRB model (blue) and the 8TRB template structure (orange), yielding a Cα RMSD of 0.335 Å. (D) Ramachandran plot of the Q99572–8TRB model. (E) Structure of 6U9W used as a template for hP2X7 model construction, with its three subunits highlighted in blue, green, and pink. queries.pdb_evidence: Results: 'Two rat P2X7 (rP2X7) receptor structures were selected as templates for modeling the hP2X7 protein: one in an ATP-bound open conformation (Protein Data Bank, PDB ID: 6U9W) and the other in an antagonist-bound closed state (PDB ID: 8TRB).' Figure 1 caption: '(A) Structure of 8TRB used as a template for hP2X7 model construction ... (E) Structure of 6U9W used as a template for hP2X7 model construction'.
queries.source_notes: MIXED - prediction compared with experiment, and explicitly a template-based (homology) model. Panels A and E are the EXPERIMENTAL rat P2X7 cryo-EM templates 8TRB (antagonist-bound closed) and 6U9W (ATP-bound open); panels B/C and F/G are the PREDICTED human P2X7 (Q99572) SWISS-MODEL homology models built on them, superposed on their templates (Calpha RMSD 0.335 A and 0.164 A). D/H are Ramachandran plots and I/J QMEANDisCo per-residue quality curves of the models. Both PDB IDs are marked partially_verified: they are the experimental templates/reference structures, NOT the depicted predicted models.
queries.caveats: Q99572-8TRB and Q99572-6U9W are homology models of a human protein built on rat templates and are not deposited in the PDB. The legacy PDB-format coordinate file for 8TRB is not served by RCSB (HTTP 404 for https://files.rcsb.org/download/8TRB.pdb); the entry's mmCIF was downloaded instead (structures/8TRB.cif) after confirming the entry exists via the RCSB data API, so no validated structures/8TRB.pdb is provided. 6U9W.pdb downloaded and validated normally. INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (partial): 8TRB and 6U9W are rat P2X7 template structures (depicted in panels A/E), while the record's subject is the human Q99572 SWISS-MODEL models, which are undeposited. The IDs are templates/reference structures, not the modelled protein.

queries.caption: Structural model of the FPPS-GPP (geranyl diphosphate) binary complex. The substrate, geranyl diphosphate (GPP), is rendered in stick form, and the magnesium ion (Mg2+) is shown as a yellow sphere. (a) Surface representation of the binary model, colored by electrostatic potential: red indicates negative, blue positive, and white neutral regions. (b) Ribbon diagram of the binary complex. queries.pdb_evidence: Figure 3 caption states the receptor model provenance: 'Ribbon diagram of the predicted FPPS structure from two orientations ... The model was predicted using AlphaFold2.' Figure 4 caption describes the complex: 'Structural model of the FPPS-GPP (geranyl diphosphate) binary complex.' Text: 'The molecular docking relied on a structure predicted using AlphaFold2, and site-specific mutagenesis was subsequently executed.' No PDB accession code is given anywhere for the FPPS model.
queries.source_notes: PREDICTED. Panel b is a ribbon diagram of the AlphaFold2-predicted M. tuberculosis FPPS in a docking-derived binary complex with geranyl diphosphate (GPP) and Mg2+; panel a is the electrostatic surface of the same model and the right-hand insets show the docked binding site. INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (partial): The Fig. 1 E/F cartoons are state 3, which the paper's data availability maps to 9EA2, but the downloaded 9EA2 coordinate file's own TITLE reads '...POLYMERASE EXCHANGE STATE 2' and 9E5Y's TITLE reads 'STATE 1' (the paper calls 9E5Y state 2). The paper and the deposited files therefore disagree on state numbering, and 9E5Y (state 1) is not the state-3 model drawn in E/F.

queries.caption: The Structure of the B 6 P 5 Form of the E. coli DnaB–lambdaP Loader. Linear domain architecture of lambdaP ( A ) and E. coli DnaB ( B ). The amino (N-terminal domain, NTD) and carboxy-terminal (C-terminal domain, CTD) layers of DnaB are depicted, with CTDs represented as large spheres and NTDs as small spheres/cylinders. ( C ) The DnaB–lambdaP complex, with its five loader molecules (labeled V, W, X, Y, and Z), is depicted in the ribbon representation and colored in shades of blue, save for chain Z, which is colored by domain as illustrated in panel (A), and in the multi-colored bracket. The right-handed open spiral of DnaB is depicted as a surface. The DnaB NTD tier is colored in dark gray, and the CTD layer is in light gray, with the DH and LH elements colored and labeled in orange and yellow. The extent of the lambdaP domain I for chains V, W, X, and Y, which are not visible in our maps, is depicted as spheres in the same color as the segments that could be modeled. ( D ) Same as panel (C), except that DnaB is depicted using spheres/cylinders as described in panel (B). The CTD spheres of each subunit carry labels corresponding to the underlying chain.
queries.pdb_evidence: Data availability: 'Coordinates from the X-ray structure of lambdaP-domain III and the cryo-EM structure of the E. coli DnaB-lambdaP complex are available from the RCSB Protein Data Bank under accession codes 8V9S (lambdaP-domain III), 8V9T (B6P5-2.84 A), 9OA1 (B6P5-2.66 A), and 9OA2 (B6P6-3.85 A).' (C) The DnaB-lambdaP complex, with its five loader molecules ... is depicted in the ribbon representation and colored in shades of blue ...' Figure 2 depicts B6P5, hence 9OA1 (2.66 A refinement of B6P5), 8V9T (the 2.84 A B6P5 cryo-EM entry) and 8V9S (the lambdaP domain III crystal structure used to build the loader).
queries.source_notes: Figure 2C is the ribbon representation of the open-spiral DnaB-lambdaP complex (loader chains V, W, X, Y, Z); panel D shows the same model with DnaB CTDs as spheres and NTDs as cylinders. Figure 1 of the same paper is a schematic pathway diagram rather than a ribbon figure and was not recorded.
queries.caveats: The B6P6 form (9OA2) is shown in Figure 9, not in this figure, so 9OA2 was not downloaded. The figure includes regions that were not visible in the map (lambdaP domain I of chains V-Y), drawn as spheres rather than ribbon. INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (partial): Fig. 2 is the B6P5 form at 2.66 A: the source says the 2.66 A map 'provides a nearly complete model' (Fig. 2) while the 2.84 A B6P5 model 'is discussed in the Supplementary Information'. So 9OA1 is the depicted entry, whereas 8V9T (2.84 A) is a supplementary refinement and 8V9S is the lambdaP domain-III crystal structure used as a modelling input - neither is the structure drawn in Fig. 2C/D.

queries.caption: Cryo-EM structures of RAD51 D-loop complexes capturing distinct heteroduplex base-pair triplet states. a – e D-loop complex containing a ⅓–1 base-pair triplet heteroduplex, ( f – i ) D-loop complex with a 2 and ⅔ base-pair triplet, ( j – m ) D-loop complex with a ⅓–3–⅔ base-pair triplet. The invading ssDNA is shown in red, and the homologous regions (8 bp or 12 bp) on the dsDNA are highlighted. The green bases represent the displaced strand. b , g , k Atomic models of RAD51–DNA complexes illustrating progressive heteroduplex formation at different triplet stages. Nucleotide sequences are labeled to show specific base-pairing events. c , h , l Ribbon diagrams of the RAD51 D-loop complexes highlighting the heteroduplex core. The ssDNA, displaced strand, and complementary strand are colored red, green, and blue, respectively. Key RAD51 residues involved in DNA interaction are shown as stick-and-ball: S2 site residues in gray, L2 loop residues in yellow, N-terminal domain (NTD) residues in orange, and Arg235 in cyan. Corresponding RAD51 protomers are labeled as superscripts. d , i , m Close-up views of protein–DNA interactions near the strand separation site. – ( d ) Interactions of Met278 N+6 ,Phe279 N+6 , and Arg306 N+7 with the just-separated displaced strand. – ( i ) Interactions of Arg235 N+6 , M278 N+7 , F279 N+7 , and Arg306 N+8 with the just-separated displaced and complementary strands. – ( m ) Interactions involving Arg235 N+6 , M278 N+7 , F279 N+7 , M278 N+8 , F279 N+8 , and Arg306 N+8 with the just-separated displaced and complementary strands.

Caption Fig. 3: '(c,h,l) Ribbon diagrams of the RAD51 D-loop complexes highlighting ...' and '(k) ... The corresponding cryo-EM structure was determined at a resolution of 3.42 A.' 9UI4 is the presynaptic RAD51 filament (2.91 A) that is the starting state; 9UI9 is the 12-bp D-loop complex (3.42 A) shown in the lower panels of Fig. 3.
queries.source_notes: Fig. 3 is a tall multi-panel figure: panels a/f/j give the DNA sequences, b/g/k the atomic models, c/h/l the ribbon diagrams at progressive heteroduplex triplet stages. Figure 4 and 5 of the same paper are molecular-dynamics simulations (predicted) and were not recorded as ribbon figures.
queries.caveats: The 4-bp and 8-bp D-loop models (9UI7, 9UI8) and the post-synaptic filament (9UI5) were not downloaded; only the two states that bracket the Fig. 3 series (presynaptic start and 12-bp D-loop end) are included. queries.paper_title: Antigenic structural analysis of bat and human norovirus protruding (P) domains
queries.caption: Four human and one bat norovirus X-ray crystal structures and a corresponding P domain sequence alignment. (A) The P domains of GII.9, GII.23, GII.27, GVIII, and GX are shown in cartoon representation. The asterisks indicated missing residues in the structure, likely due to the flexibility of the loop. The P domain, subdivided into P1 and P2 subdomains, is colored chain A P1/chain B P1 and chain A P2/chain B P2 for GII.9 (sand/ light blue and deep purple/split pea), GII.23 (purple/ brown and salmon/ light blue), GII.27 (lime green/ firebrick and deep blue/ teal), GVIII (olive/ smudge and pink/ aquamarine), and GX (hot pink/ pale cyan and green/ orange), respectively. Loop A is located near the HBGA pocket and commonly contains the essential fucose moiety binding residue (e.g., GII.4 R345) and is longer in GII.23 (~17 residues) and GII.27 (~17 residues) than in GII.9 (~9 residues), GVIII (~9 residues), and GX (~8 residues). (B) Clustal W sequence alignment showing the partial P domains of GII.9, GII.23, GII.27, GVIII, GX, and with consensus GII.4 (Syd-2012, JX459908). The P2 subdomains contain numerous insertions and deletions compared to the P1 subdomains. Loop A (pink highlight) and two regular HBGA binding residues in GII.4 P domains (R345 and D374, gray highlight, and termed FUC) are shown. The two equivalent residues in the GII.9 (R346 and D374), GII.23 (R355 and D384), and GII.27 (R355 and D384) P domain structures are positioned similarly to the GII.4 P domain. The GVIII and GX P domains lack these two residues, except for GX D367 (highlighted red), which is located on the equivalent loop and near GII.4 D374.
